ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, shareholders, directors, resident agents, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, Panama's UAF domestic financial criminal and terrorist lists, INTERPOL notices, and enhanced due diligence measures for politically exposed persons and their family members or close associates, all in accordance with Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree 363 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Servicios en Línea (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Latin-alphabet characters; non-Latin scripts are generally not accepted by the Registro Público. The corporate name must end with 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' and must be readily distinguishable from existing registered names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gobierno de la República de Panamá
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects the requested name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the name clearance section within five business days. If the reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Dirección General del Registro Público under Panama's general administrative procedure law (Law 38 of 2000). The appellant must attach a fresh name search certificate, demonstrate distinctive difference from prior registered names, and may propose an amended name to expedite approval. Judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Supreme Court remains available after exhaustion of administrative remedies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered agent's virtual office is permissible for satisfying the statutory registered office requirement. However, for a delivery-only ghost kitchen operating under ISIC 5610, the operating entity must maintain a physical commercial kitchen premises with the required municipal operating license and MINSA food safety permits. A virtual office alone is not sufficient commercial substance for the operational entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama General Corporation Law, Law No. 32 of February 26, 1927, as last amended by Laws 5 of 2017 and 70 of 2019; applicable provisions on incorporation, share capital, registered office, resident agent, and officers include Arts. 1-10, 18-25, 33, 58, and 100.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Section of the Public Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Inscripción de la Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Articles and Bylaws of a Panamanian Stock Corporation submitted through the Registry's digital platform or notarial deed).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required. The Articles of Association may state an authorized share capital of one or more shares; for nominee or non-resident formation, a subscribed capital schedule is prepared. No paid-in capital need be physically contributed or deposited prior to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation subscribes and accepts the share subscription schedule submitted to this Board, satisfies all statutory minimum capital requirements insofar as required by Panamanian law, and adopts as its registered office the address identified in the Articles of Incorporation, with effect immediately. RESOLVED, that the persons named in the officer schedule are appointed President, Secretary, Treasurer and Resident Agent, each to hold office until their respective successors are elected and duly qualified. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to file all requisite registrations, to open bank accounts, to apply for health, environmental and fire licensing, and to execute any ancillary instruments necessary to commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and Preliminary Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Name Verification Section (Quórum / Sistema de Verificación de Nombres)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three ranked proposed corporate names through the Registry's online name search module or through the corporate agent's official interface. The name must end in 'S.A.' or otherwise comply with Panamanian law and must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name. After clearance, the name approval certificate is issued and reserved for the statutory formation filing.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names in Spanish
Corporate agent or nominee shareholder identification
Basic beneficial ownership declaration form
Name clearance application fee (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected or abusively similar, the filer receives a formal objection note. Remedy: submit substitute names within 5 business days through the same online module; no administrative hearing is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Incorporation before a Panama Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Panamá (Public Notary) and/or the corporate service law firm authorized to sign electronically
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social / Estatutos) before a licensed Panamanian Notary. The instrument appoints the Resident Agent, establishes the registered office address, describes the share classes and subscribed capital, names the initial directors and officers, and defines the corporate object (operation of delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen facilities). Notarization must be completed prior to registry submission.
required_dossiers: Name clearance certificate (última boleta de nombre, if applicable)
Passport copies and corporate details of shareholders/directors
Resident Agent acceptance letter
Registered office address documentation
Proposed capital schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues an objection due to missing documentation or statutory incompleteness, the practitioner corrects the draft and re-notarizes. A notarially certified original showing no erasures or interlineations must be produced; failure requires a fresh notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Registration with the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil / Online Fiduciary and Corporate Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Incorporation, together with the registered office declaration and Resident Agent appointment, via the Registry's transactional platform or in-person window. The Registry reviews conformity, causes publication of the Matrícula Mercantil (if required), and issues a Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Inscripción / Personería Jurídica). Payment of the statutory registration fee and municipal stamp duty is made at this stage.
required_dossiers: Notarized original Articles of Incorporation
Resident Agent appointment letter and identity documents
Registered office address confirmation
Proof of payment of registration fees
Beneficial ownership declaration (as required under non-resident registration rules)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a preventive note or corrective note, the filer will cure the cited defect within 10 business days, paying any deficiency assessment; failure to respond within the statutory period may result in cancellation of the filing. If refused, the filer may re-file corrected documents without substantial delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Taxpayer Identification (RUC) and Municipal Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, and Municipalidad / Alcaldía of the district where the ghost kitchen operates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, file for the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) by submitting corporate registration certificate and director/shareholder identity documents. Simultaneously, request the Municipal Aviso de Operación for the registered office and kitchen facility; the municipality will verify that the premises comply with zoning, occupancy, and road access requirements. For a delivery-only business, the Aviso de Operación should note the exclusive delivery-warehouse nature.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporation Registration
RUC application form and identity documents of legal representative
Copies of municipal property/tax payment receipts (if available)
Proof of registered office and kitchen premises address
Prospective health and fire inspection approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality objects due to zoning or sanitation concerns, the operator may submit an amended Aviso de Operación with a narrower business description or obtain a special use variance from the Municipal Council. DGI tax identification issues are curable through online portal correction if the RUC form has typographical discrepancies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Completion of Corporate Records, Registered Office and Resident Agent Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Agent / Resident Agent and the Registry's Electronic Registry of Shareholders and Directors (maintained privately at the resident agent's office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and maintain the statutory corporate records book, including the Certificate of Registration, Articles, bylaws, first Board Resolutions, share ledger, registered office adoption statement, and appointment of officers. In Panama, the shareholder and director registers are not publicly filed; they are maintained by the Resident Agent. The Resident Agent must accept service of process and maintain accountability for unreported beneficial owners under the beneficial ownership reporting rules.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Articles of Incorporation
Copy of the First Board Resolution
Share subscription and ownership ledger
Director and officer registers
Resident Agent acceptance and confidentiality undertaking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Resident Agent detects missing documentation, the board will execute curative resolutions. If the Registry requires proof of registered office maintenance, the agent files a Reglamento de Oficina Registrada with updated address; failure to maintain an active registered office can trigger cancellation of the corporate existence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA), Dirección General de Salud Pública; Subsecretaría de Alimentos y Bebidas; Municipalidad de Panamá
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Operación para Establecimiento de Preparación y Entrega de Alimentos (Permiso Sanitario for Food Preparation and Delivery-Only Operation)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II (Registration with Environmental Diagnostic Report) – low-impact food service establishment; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Categoría III is not required, but a diagnostic report detailing waste generation, wastewater characteristics, cooking emissions and energy consumption must be filed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary sewage discharges to municipal sewer must comply with Panamanian standards for wastewater: pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 not exceeding 250 mg/L, COD not exceeding 400 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 250 mg/L, and fat/oil/grease not exceeding 50 mg/L. Cooking exhaust must pass through acceptable grease extraction and filtered ventilation systems; volatile organic compounds and combustion gases must remain within Panamanian ambient air quality parameters. Solid waste and used cooking oil must be handled through certified waste haulers; waste separation and disposal must follow MiAMBIENTE and Municipal waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification and Pre-Operation Inspection from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, confirming fire suppressions systems, exit signage, extinguishers, and commercial kitchen exhaust hood protection; structural load verification and zoning compliance from the Municipal Engineering Department; and workplace occupational safety and health clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), covering electrical safety, ventilation, employee hygiene, handling of hazardous cleaning chemicals, and ergonomic work stations for delivery staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) of the Republic of Panama. Official electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa, providing the e-RUC, e-filing, electronic invoice validation, and taxpayer management systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima: (1) duly incorporate before a Panama notary and register the corporate charter with the Public Registry; (2) file the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Business Operation) at the DGI within 30 days of commencing commercial activity; (3) obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), which serves simultaneously for income tax and ITBMS; (4) for a branch of a non-Panamanian corporation, deposit an apostilled certificate of incorporation, by-laws, and board resolution appointing a local agent; (5) activate the online account in the DGI Sede Electrónica using a digital signature certificate issued by an authorized certifying authority; (6) request the applicable invoice series and taxpayer e-credentials. Non-resident shareholders must submit passport copies or a foreign tax identification number for the transparency register. No minimum capital or local residency of shareholders is statutorily required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope; Entity_Level_Taxation. A Panamanian S.A. is a separate juridical person subject to entity-level corporate income tax at 25% only on income derived from Panamanian-source activities and assets; all foreign-source income received by the S.A. is outside the Panamanian tax net. The entity is not a pass-through vehicle and has no check-the-box analogue to disregarded LLC status for Panamanian tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no U.S.-style check-the-box election and no general hybrid-mismatch election. Available statutory elections include: (i) the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) special regime under Law 41 of 2007, subject to meeting headcount, payroll, and regional-export requirements, replacing ordinary corporate income tax with an annual fixed tax; (ii) exclusive territorial fiscal regimes applicable to companies physically operating in the Panama Pacifico and City of Knowledge designated areas; (iii) the Simplified Tax Regime (REST) for small taxpayers whose annual gross revenue is within the statutory cap; and (iv) automatic territorial-source treatment for foreign-derived income, provided the taxpayer maintains documentary proof that the income was generated outside Panama and invoiced to non-domiciled counterparties.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / ITBMS — Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y la Prestación de Servicios. The general rate is 7%; exports are zero-rated; certain prepared-food restaurant or catering activities, alcoholic beverages, and tobacco products may attract special rates as established by DGI regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 0 — Panama imposes no general de minimis turnover threshold for ITBMS registration. Every person or entity engaged in taxable commercial activity in Panama must register for ITBMS from the first taxable transaction. Small taxpayers whose annual gross income does not exceed the statutory simplified-regime limit may elect the REST regime, but this does not eliminate the basic RUC/ITBMS registration requirement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a mandatory electronic invoicing framework under the DGI 'Facturación Electrónica' system. All RUC-registered taxpayers must issue fiscal invoices in electronic form. The DGI authorises chronological invoice series; invoices must be transmitted to the DGI via the Sede Electrónica or an approved API connector. For each transaction, the system performs digital validation and returns a fiscal authorization code/QR stamp. Real-time fiscal clearance is mandatory for large taxpayers and is being phased in for all registered businesses. Credit notes and debit notes must be processed through the same electronic clearance loop, and the original XML/PDF electronic file must be retained for the statutory retention period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating at 0% ITBMS is available for: (i) tangible goods physically exported from Panama to a foreign destination, provided the goods leave Panamanian customs territory under a valid export declaration; and (ii) services sold to a non-resident or non-domiciled customer where the benefit, use, and consumption occur entirely outside Panama. Eligibility requires that the invoice identifies the RUC of the Panamanian exporter, quotes ITBMS at 0%, and that the exporter maintains direct evidence of the foreign sale, the payment inflow, and the export movement. For a ghost kitchen or virtual-brand operator, true cross-border catering or delivery to non-Panamanian recipients abroad may qualify, whereas local delivery orders from platforms such as UberEats or DoorDash are domestic supplies subject to the applicable Panamanian ITBMS rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas / Export Manifest DU)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing physical departure from Panama
Commercial Invoice (Factura Comercial) quoting RUC and 0% ITBMS
Freight forwarder certificate or shipping document showing final foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice demonstrating FX repatriation
Service contract and certificate of non-residence of the foreign buyer (for service exports)
Container or seal number records in the name of the Panamanian exporter (for goods exports)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI maintains a dedicated export zero-rating audit program that cross-checks the National Customs Authority export registries, bank inward-remittance records, and the exporter's RUC filings. If a zero-rated invoice lacks the mandatory customs or remittance support, DGI will recharacterise the supply as taxable domestically and assess the omitted 7% (or applicable special-rate) ITBMS. The exporter may then be subject to a 100% administrative surcharge on the under-declared tax, statutory monthly interest, and fines of up to 200% of the omitted tax for intentional fraud. Fraudulent export schemes carry criminal tax-evasion liability under Panamanian law with potential imprisonment, forfeiture of refunded VAT/ITBMS credits, and retroactive clawback for the statutory assessment window, which is extended in cases of false documentation or deliberate concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama); Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas) — Panama has no central bank and uses the US Dollar as legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama has a fully dollarized financial system with no exchange controls; the US Dollar is sole legal tender. Both capital and current account transactions are freely convertible, with no quantitative restrictions on the conversion, repatriation, or remittance of profits. Legal and judicial protections ensure prompt transferability of funds. Practical hurdles are limited to satisfying AML/KYC requirements and documentary evidence of the underlying transaction. Dividends attached to bearer shares are disallowed, and profits remitted may be subject to a 10% dividend tax (or applicable tax treaty relief), but no convertibility or surrender restrictions exist.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory obligation exists for exporters to surrender export proceeds or convert foreign currency receipts into local currency. Because Panama's monetary system adopts the US Dollar, all exported proceeds may be retained in USD or any other foreign currency, freely deposited, held, or remitted. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, no timeline for repatriation, and no central bank control.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium feasibility. Panama does not currently grant deposit-taking authorizations to pure digital EMIs; non-bank fintech companies must operate under a banking license or as a licensed payment processor. Offshore EMIs cannot perform banking or deposit-taking activities in Panama and cannot hold client funds in Panama without a local license. As an alternative, ghost kitchen operators may establish a Panama corporate account in a tier-1 bank for local currency (USD) operations, while using an offshore fintech (e.g., a US or EU EMI) for international disbursements if compliant with local AML regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors, beneficial shareholders, and authorized signatories are generally required to be physically present at a Panamanian bank branch or recognized representative office to complete a personal interview, provide original IDs, and sign the account opening forms. Remote opening is rarely accepted for non-resident entities; a private banking manager must verify biometrics, and corporate documents must be apostilled and legalized. The in-person interview may be waived only in exceptional pre-approved arrangements through a correspondent bank or for highly rated inward investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual source of wealth for initial capital injection or subsequent large cash deposits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarized and apostilled source of wealth documentation, audited financial statements of the parent entity, bank reference letters, tax returns, and a comprehensive board resolution explaining the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate vehicle is a Panama S.A. with a bearer share history or bearer share-like structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a share register (Registro de Accionistas) and certificate of no bearer shares, current corporate documents showing the exact legal representative chain, and beneficial ownership declaration as required by Panama's tax transparency regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between business object and transactional pattern (e.g., ghost kitchen claiming high restaurant revenue without physical storefront).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the statutory operating license (Aviso de Operación), municipal business license, health and fire safety permits, physical lease or utility bills, delivery platform agreements (Uber Eats, DoorDash), and a detailed operational matrix proving active virtual brand kitchen operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to or from high-risk jurisdictions or tax havens.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide underlying commercial contracts, invoices, and bill of lading / customs declarations; maintain the correct SWIFT purpose codes; and provide an economic substance folder evidencing compliance with unlimited-to-foreign-tax liability rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account signatory is a nominee or proxy without clear beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully disclose ultimate beneficial owners, provide passport copies, proof of address, and a formal corporate authorization power, ensuring beneficial owners are expressly named in the AML/CFT forms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use an SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire transfer from the parent shareholder's account in a reputable jurisdiction. The payment must reference the corporate RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and clearly state the purpose code: 'Equity injection / direct investment' (BPM6 code E511 for equity). Verification requires a board resolution approving the capital call, a notarized capital contribution certificate, registration with the Registro Público (if increasing authorized capital), and a sworn statement of the source of funds to satisfy AML. Funds must land in the named corporate account; the bank will free it after completing verification of accounts and OFAC screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements are executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments, Commercial LC (MT700) for substantial import settlements (e.g., kitchen equipment), and local ACH for domestic payroll and vendor payments. The bank treasury issues the payment after matching the beneficiary KYC, the underlying invoice/trade document, and the applicable purpose code (services, goods, royalties). Settlement is cleared in USD through Panama's local clearing house or internationally via correspondent banks, primarily with the Federal Reserve.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign exchange spot and outright forwards via offshore banks
No local Panama FX derivatives market due to full dollarization; hedging is executed offshore

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto Anual de Sociedades (Annual Corporate Franchise Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers 10% penalty plus 1% monthly interest; continued non-payment leads to suspension of registration rights and eventual strike-off after 3 consecutive years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Jurada Anual de Renta (Annual Income Tax Return – Form 201)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the following fiscal year (for December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of 10% of the tax determined, plus monthly interest; failure to file for 3 years allows administrative strike-off and immigration blacklisting for directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit condition: annual gross revenue exceeding USD 3 million or total assets exceeding USD 3 million, as determined by the DGI for tax-registered corporations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) as adopted in Panama; smaller entities may use PCGA (locally adapted GAAP).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All SAs must maintain a Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (RBF) on-site and provide annual written confirmation to the registered agent; any shareholding transfer triggers an update within 30 days. The annual confirmation is not a public filing but must be produced for DGI/Registro Público inspection upon request.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive corporate income tax (ISR) for fiscal years 2025 onward: 19% on the first PAB 100,000 of net taxable income; 25% on taxable income from PAB 100,001 to PAB 1,000,000; 27% on taxable income exceeding PAB 1,000,000. The former flat 25% statutory rate is fully replaced by the progressive bands.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday, investment allowance, or sector-specific CIT incentive applies to ghost kitchen or virtual brand operations. Panama's territorial tax regime excludes foreign-source revenue from the Panamanian tax base, but the delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen derives Panama-source revenue from local food sales and platform payouts. The Multinational Headquarters (SEM), Export Services (ESE), and Panama-Pacific regimes are not available to a domestically focused delivery operator. Standard deductions for operating costs are available; ITBMS (Panama's value-added tax of 7%) is a separate indirect tax obligation and must not be netted against the ISR base.
